boardMaterials.name: End-Grain Hard Rock Maple (Acer saccharum)
boardMaterials.capillaryAbsorptionRate: High (Vertical xylem capillaries absorb fluids internally within 3-10 minutes)
boardMaterials.desiccationKinetics: Rapid (Natural xylem dehydration kills >99.9% bacteria within 3-12 hours)
boardMaterials.tanninPhenolicContent: Moderate (Gallic & ellagic acid precursors inhibit microbial cell membranes)
boardMaterials.knifeSelfHealing: Superior (Knife cuts between vertical fibers rather than severing them)
boardMaterials.description: The gold standard of commercial and residential culinary cutting boards. Vertical wood pores draw fluid and bacterial cells deep into the porous interior via capillary action, separating bacteria from food contact surfaces where natural dehydration and wood phytochemicals lead to bacterial death.

boardMaterials.name: Edge-Grain Plantation Teak (Tectona grandis)
boardMaterials.capillaryAbsorptionRate: Low-Moderate (High natural silica & hydrophobic oleoresin content slows fluid uptake)
boardMaterials.desiccationKinetics: Moderate (Natural tectoquinones provide durable bacteriostatic inhibition)
boardMaterials.tanninPhenolicContent: Very High (Tectoquinones and natural waxes prevent deep microbial penetration)
boardMaterials.knifeSelfHealing: Moderate (Dense natural oily surface resists gouging, gentle on knife edges)
boardMaterials.description: Rich in natural oils and silica, teak possesses inherent water resistance and mold-repelling properties. While it absorbs less moisture than maple, its dense resin matrix actively suppresses bacterial proliferation and resists surface waterlogging.

boardMaterials.name: End-Grain Acacia (Acacia mangium / mangium hybrid)
boardMaterials.capillaryAbsorptionRate: Moderate-High (Fibrous vascular bundles with fast capillary draw)
boardMaterials.desiccationKinetics: Very Rapid (High condensed tannins accelerate microbial cell wall breakdown)
boardMaterials.tanninPhenolicContent: Extreme (Rich in proanthocyanidins and complex polyphenols)
boardMaterials.knifeSelfHealing: High (Hard end-grain yields under blade contact, closing micro-cuts)
boardMaterials.description: Extremely hard and resilient with dense tannin concentrations. End-grain acacia rapidly desiccates moisture from trapped pathogens. Its high tannin content acts as a natural antimicrobial preservative, significantly accelerating Salmonella and Campylobacter die-off.

boardMaterials.name: Laminated Moso Bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis)
boardMaterials.capillaryAbsorptionRate: Low (Dense outer culm, but porous longitudinal vascular bundles)
boardMaterials.desiccationKinetics: Low-Moderate (Slow natural drying once water penetrates glue joints)
boardMaterials.knifeSelfHealing: Poor (Fibrous surface splinters; requires aggressive cutting pressure)
boardMaterials.description: Composed of bamboo strips bonded with synthetic adhesives (urea-formaldehyde or melamine PVA glue). While moisture-resistant initially, knife gouges fracture longitudinal fibers and expose glue seams where moisture traps bacteria and causes delamination over time.

boardMaterials.name: Scratched High-Density Polyethylene Plastic (HDPE Control)
boardMaterials.capillaryAbsorptionRate: Zero (100% Non-porous synthetic plastic; all fluid pools on surface)
boardMaterials.desiccationKinetics: None (Trapped fluids remain wet for days in humid kitchen air)
boardMaterials.tanninPhenolicContent: Zero (Inert synthetic polyolefin; no natural antimicrobial activity)
boardMaterials.knifeSelfHealing: Zero (Permanent plastic feathered gouges create micro-caves and burrs)
boardMaterials.description: Non-porous culinary plastic. Knife cuts feather into microscopic hanging plastic flaps and deep trenches. Bacteria cannot penetrate into the material, remaining pooled on the surface protected inside knife scars where kitchen sponges and light dish soap cannot physically dislodge them.

pathogens.name: Salmonella enterica (Poultry Serovars)
pathogens.naturalMortalityOnDryWood: High (99% die-off within 3–6 hours on dry hardwood)
pathogens.biofilmPotential: High (Forms cellulose-curli fimbriae biofilms on scratched plastic)
pathogens.clinicalHazard: Severe gastrointestinal infection, bacteremia, dehydration, reactive arthritis

pathogens.name: Campylobacter jejuni (Raw Poultry Juice)
pathogens.naturalMortalityOnDryWood: Extreme (Obligate microaerophilic; dies rapidly on drying wood within 60–120 mins)
pathogens.clinicalHazard: Acute enteritis, bloody diarrhea, Guillain-Barré syndrome auto-immune paralysis

pathogens.name: Escherichia coli O157:H7 (STEC / Raw Beef)
pathogens.naturalMortalityOnDryWood: Moderate-High (Desiccates within 4–8 hours on dry maple)
pathogens.clinicalHazard: Shiga-toxin mediated hemorrhagic colitis, Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS) kidney failure

pathogens.name: Listeria monocytogenes (Deli Meat & Seafood)
pathogens.naturalMortalityOnDryWood: Moderate (Halotolerant, psychrotrophic; slower desiccation than Campylobacter)
pathogens.clinicalHazard: Invasive listeriosis, meningitis, fetal loss / miscarriage in pregnant women

pathogens.name: Staphylococcus aureus (Skin & Cook Contact)
pathogens.naturalMortalityOnDryWood: Moderate (Gram-positive peptidoglycan cell wall tolerates partial drying)
pathogens.clinicalHazard: Heat-stable enterotoxin emetic intoxication, rapid projectile vomiting (1–6 hrs)

boardWearConditions.name: Pristine / Properly Seasoned & Mineral-Oiled
boardWearConditions.surfaceCondition: Smooth uniform wood, sealed pores, hydrophobic beading, zero feathered gouges

boardWearConditions.name: Moderate Residential Use (Minor Knife Scoring)
boardWearConditions.surfaceCondition: Surface shallow cuts (0.3–0.6 mm deep), partial oil loss, light grain lifting

boardWearConditions.name: Heavily Scored & Deeply Grooved (Years of Cleaver Work)
boardWearConditions.surfaceCondition: Deep overlapping knife crevices (>1.5 mm), fraying wood fibers, unconditioned bone-dry wood

boardWearConditions.name: Cracked Seams / Delaminated Joints (Dishwasher Traumatized)
boardWearConditions.surfaceCondition: Open hairline cracks between laminations, deep moisture trapping, permanent wet core

sanitizationProtocols.name: Ambient Air-Drying Only (12h Clean Benchtop)
sanitizationProtocols.description: Rinsed with warm water and allowed to dry vertically on an open drying rack for 12 hours. Capillary action pulls pathogens into wood xylem where water evaporates and bacteria desiccate. On plastic, lack of absorption leaves surface bacteria viable in moisture drops.

sanitizationProtocols.name: Dish Soap Scrub + Hot Water (>50°C / 122°F)
sanitizationProtocols.woodDamageRisk: Low (Strip oils slightly; requires periodic re-waxing)
sanitizationProtocols.description: Standard hand-washing with heavy brush scrub and dish soap. Surfactant emulsifies surface fats and bacterial membranes. Highly effective on smooth wood and plastic, but brush bristles cannot reach the bottom of 1.5mm deep plastic cuts.

sanitizationProtocols.name: Dilute Bleach Sanitizing Soak (200 ppm NaOCl)
sanitizationProtocols.woodDamageRisk: Moderate (Bleaches natural wood pigment; degrades lignin over time)
sanitizationProtocols.description: 1 tablespoon unscented household bleach per gallon of water (approx. 200 ppm free chlorine). Left on surface for 5–10 minutes. Penetrates knife scars on plastic and oxidizes microbial cell walls.

sanitizationProtocols.name: Sequential 3% Hydrogen Peroxide & 5% White Vinegar Spray
sanitizationProtocols.woodDamageRisk: Very Low (Food safe, non-toxic, doesn't strip wood oils)
sanitizationProtocols.description: Mist surface thoroughly with 3% hydrogen peroxide, let sit 2 minutes, then mist with 5% white vinegar and wipe clean. Creates peracetic acid in situ, demonstrating 10x greater bactericidal efficacy than either compound alone.

sanitizationProtocols.name: Automatic Dishwasher (High-Temp Wash + Heated Dry)
sanitizationProtocols.woodDamageRisk: Catastrophic on Wood (Warps, splits glue joints, cracks, ruins hardwood)
sanitizationProtocols.description: 140°F–160°F wash with concentrated metasilicates and heated dry cycle. Complete thermal kill. Safe ONLY for plastic and composite NSF boards. Destroys solid wood boards within 1–3 cycles by rupturing cellular glue bonds.

sanitizationProtocols.name: Cold Water & Dirty Sponge / Dishcloth Wipe Down
sanitizationProtocols.woodDamageRisk: High (Traps damp bacterial biofilm without adequate ventilation)
sanitizationProtocols.description: The most dangerous common practice: wiping down a meat-contaminated board with a damp kitchen rag or sponge. Re-inoculates the board surface with coliforms and spreads pathogens across every cutting zone.

cliverStudyBenchmarks.woodRecoveryAfter3Hours: 0.1% of inoculated bacteria recoverable from surface (99.9% reduction)
cliverStudyBenchmarks.plasticRecoveryAfter3Hours: 100% to 150% of inoculated bacteria recoverable from surface (active growth in juice drops)
cliverStudyBenchmarks.mineralOilEfficacy: Mineral oil saturation forms a hydrophobic moisture barrier, preventing meat blood from soaking deeper than 1mm while maintaining fiber elasticity
